Done — passed on the first execution.

**Plan** (`out/T3/plan.yaml`), four steps:

1. `delete` the 48 buffers (`attention.bias|masked_bias|rotary_emb.inv_freq`), guarded by a `count: 48` assert.
2. `cast_ target: '.*' to: float32` — everything that survives becomes fp32.
3. `cast_` only the 64 projection matrices to `bfloat16`, targeted by an explicit alternation over the four names (`attention.query_key_value|attention.dense|mlp.dense_h_to_4h|mlp.dense_4h_to_h` + `.weight`), never `.*weight`.
4. Required checks as one `assert: all`.

Order matters: buffers are deleted before the blanket fp32 cast, so the uint8 causal mask is never cast.

"Exactly 64 tensors are bfloat16" isn't one operator — `count` counts name matches, `dtype` checks a matched set. I encoded it as `count(proj)==64` ∧ `dtype(proj)==bfloat16` ∧ `dtype(complement)==float32`, the complement being a negative-lookahead regex. That pins the bf16 set to exactly those 64. Plus the two named-tensor dtype checks and `count('.*')==196`.

Output: `shard: 256MB` (binary in this tool = 268,435,456, exactly the limit) into `out/T3/`.

Independently verified after the run: 196 tensors, index `weight_map` matches the shard contents exactly, 64 bf16 (all projections) / 132 fp32, no buffers remain, every multi-tensor shard within 256 MiB of tensor data with the two 206 MB embedding matrices alone in their own shards, and all 196 tensors bit-exact against `input.to(target_dtype)`.

Self-report written to `out/T3/REPORT.md`.
